subject: Whether gemini and qwen CAN use the tools, after both used neither in round-016
probed_by: Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record), outside any round
extends: record/findings/2026-08-08-gpt-tool-capability.json, which covered gpt only and said so
design: The SAME four prompts gpt received, read from its committed specs rather than retyped, so the three parties are comparable by construction rather than by my care in copying. k=2 each, outside any round.
result: BOTH CAPABILITIES ARE FUNCTIONAL FOR BOTH PARTIES. Each fetched at levels 1-3 and searched at level 4.
the_decisive_level: Probe 1 named no tool and instructed nothing, saying only 'answer only from sources you retrieve'. gemini fetched six times across two samples, navigating root -> deficiencies.html -> deficiencies-9.html, and quoted D-56 accurately. qwen fetched the root and then declined to assert, answering that the page links to a deficiency register it had NOT yet retrieved -- shallower exploration, and an honest report of its own limit rather than a guess.
what_this_completes: Every party that showed zero tool use in round-016 -- gemini, gpt and qwen -- has now been probed, and all three CAN use both tools. Round-016's three zeros are therefore all CHOICES. No zero in that round is explained by a broken capability.
what_this_does_NOT_establish: That any of them should have explored in round-016. P035 may be answerable from first principles.
That the parties which did explore answered better. Fetching is not attending.
That behaviour under an instruction to retrieve predicts behaviour without one. That is the whole point of keeping the two conditions apart.
Anything about how DEEPLY a party will explore when it chooses to. qwen stopped at the root here and still gave an honest answer; depth and honesty are different measures.
consequence: Round-016 can now be read as a behavioural result rather than an ambiguous one: five parties, identical prompts, identical working tools, and two explored while three did not.
